_comment: Scatter: sparse work-clutter only at stations per direction.md, but no bespoke ingot/tool-rack sprite is picked yet ('future picks')
interior_flavor: Nothing there. Warm metal underfoot, and a rhythm below it that never quite stops.
Nothing there. Scale on the flags and the smell of hot iron.
_comment_cover_skip: cover_skip exposes the molten seam art; the five cells remain blocked.

floor_layers._comment: MAP/PALLASS-FORGE-FLOOR: wall rows 0-1 and the walkable brick were one texture. Row 2 takes the slate band row 9 uses, framing the floor dark top and bottom. No blocking moves.
the brick_over_molten atlas's all-lower molten cell (id0 [0,0]) painted ONLY at the 5 seam cells (paired with `cover_skip` above so the dark blocked overlay skips them).

_comment_scatter: v0.15 T4.1: the tier's floor read as swept-empty slate between stations. Mill scale and scrap, drifted the way a working floor drifts (the street/floodplains scatter idiom, presentation-only).

entities.observe: A workbench of calipers, weights, and chalk lines — every tool squared to the bench edge. The Magus is up at the office when he is not down here.
entities.toast: Every tool squared to the bench edge. You decide against touching anything.

entities.observe: An anvil bolted to its own slab, a furnace mouth banked low beside it — cold for now, but built to run hot for a working day at a time.
entities.toast: The metal underfoot still holds the day's heat, hours after the last hammer fell.
entities._light_comment: v0.17 R2: 0.8@26 -> 1.05@42, so the banked mouth reaches the floor of a 26-cell tier.

entities.observe: A second bench, same pattern as the first — built to the same civic spec as the market tier's stalls, just built for heat instead of trade.
entities.toast: Tool racks, empty for the moment, and the bench still ticking as it cools.
entities._light_comment: v0.17 R2: the tier's second banked mouth. Count 7 -> 8 = LIGHT_BUDGET, so this map is FULL.

entities.observe: A bronze grate exhales a slow white breath, steady as a held note. Somewhere below, something enormous is always working.
entities.toast: Warm, damp air. A rhythm underneath it, too even to be weather.

entities.observe: A bronze-riveted cage, tall enough to swallow a wagon, counterweights racked in a shaft that drops past sight.
entities.locked_toast: The brass gate is locked. A stencilled plate: PERMIT AND STAMP REQUIRED. The clerk's window is open.

door_when.open_toast: The brass gate rises with a well-oiled clank, counterweights turning smooth in their track. The lift carries you down, into the ordered quiet of the market tier.

entities._comment: respawns:true, MEASURED-only in the harness (a first-of-its-kind region, no established band to hold).
entities._comment_tint: MAP/PALLASS-FORGE-FLOOR: the golem read as parked machinery, same purple-grey as its tier. Ember cast separates it from the brick; rig and stats untouched.
entities.observe: A stone shape stands too near the tier's own edge, cracks along its arms glowing a shade too bright for the forge-heat alone.

entities._comment: v0.15 T4.1. Pool = first-talk-of-a-waking flavor, `conversation` carries every later talk (brothers_parlor precedent). NO elevator_pass_stamped stage: the lift is the only live route onto this tier, so the gate is structurally met and the base pool IS the post-permit voice (CHOICE-LOG).
entities.observe: A Drake in a scarred leather apron, forearms banded with old burn-marks she stopped covering years ago. She works without looking up, and the work doesn't suffer for it.
entities.friendly_line: She sets the hammer down long enough to look at you properly. The billet on the anvil goes a shade darker while she does.
talk_pool: Bench is rated for a working day at a time. It gets one, and not a bell more.
Stand clear of the quench, {addr}. Steam doesn't care whose day it is.
Everything on this tier is built to the civic spec. That includes the tier.
You want a thing made, you file for it downstairs. You want to watch, stand where you are.

lines: The miscalibrated one used to drift past my slab at the third bell. It doesn't now.
I don't say thanks over a hot hammer. Take it as said.
Liscor settled the thing under its stone. Good. I'd still like the measurements.
News comes up the shaft slower than heat does. Arrives just as true.
She passed it this morning. Same hand, same steel, honest measure. Nothing else changed.
The examiner sent the file up himself. He has never once walked up a flight for me.
You did not make her better, {addr}. You made the reading true. That is the harder favor.

entities._comment: v0.15 T4.1. Brass tint on the shared `tier_clerk` rig: the uniformity IS the Pallass tell, the tint is what keeps three uniformed Drakes apart at a glance (docs/design/character-profiles.md).
entities.observe: A Drake in a brass-buttoned lift coat, one hand resting on the gate lever without gripping it. He watches the counterweights instead of the passengers, and knows where both are.
entities.friendly_line: He tips two fingers off the gate lever. "Quarter bell," he says, and puts them back.
talk_pool: Down at the quarter bell, up at the half. If you aren't sure which, wait. The bell is sure.
Mind the gate track, {addr}. It shuts on a count, not on a look.
Nine tiers under us and every one of them wants something carried. That's the whole job.
The cage takes twelve, or eight and a wagon. It has never once taken thirteen.

lines: Liscor's news rode up on the quarter-bell cage, same as the tin does.
People asked me about it all morning. I told them what I knew, then I ran the cage.
Manifest's clean. First clean manifest since the frost, and I have checked it twice for the pleasure.
Her boy rode up with a jar for me. I told him the cage takes twelve. He asked if it takes jars.
Down at the quarter bell, {addr}. Same as always. It just goes down lighter.

entities.observe: Tongs, swages and fullers hung in size order along a painted rack, every one of them chalk-outlined on the boards behind it. One outline in the middle of the row is bare.
entities.toast: You lift a set of tongs off its outline and set it back. Heavier than it looks, and it goes back exactly straight.

entities.observe: Every bench on the tier chalked in a column, the smith's mark beside it and the hours they're owed. Two marks have been rubbed out and rewritten in a different hand.
entities.toast: Bench hours, to the quarter. Nobody up here works a minute they can't account for.

entities.observe: Bar stock stacked by gauge, each bundle strapped and tagged. The tags carry a tier number, a bench number, and nothing else. No names anywhere on them.
entities.toast: Cold iron, every bar cut to the same length as the one beside it. The strapping doesn't give under your hand.

entities._comment: Sprite reads picked off the first windowed pass, not off the name: `cauldron` put a FIRE in the quench (a lit pot beside the anvil), `riverfarm_fence_ew` put WOOD against the molten seam, and a second `barrel` cloned the quench 7 cells away. Barrel/boulder/rail-at-the-parapet is what the tier actually reads as.
entities.observe: A standing barrel of water beside the anvil, skinned over with scale and grey all the way down. The rim is worn smooth in the two places a smith's hands go.
entities.toast: The water is warmer than the room around it. Something went in here not long ago.

entities.observe: Cooled slag and cracked crucible shards, heaped no higher than a line painted on the flagstones around it. The line has been repainted recently, and brightly.
entities.toast: Glassy black waste, still holding a little of the day's heat. Even the refuse up here has a level marked on it.

entities.observe: A bronze rail along the tier's open edge, polished bright by a hundred people leaning on the same stretch of it while they waited on the cage. Below it the shaft goes down past where the light gives up.
entities.toast: You put a hand on the rail. Warm from the tier, not from the drop, and it does not shift at all under your weight.

entities._comment: v0.15 T4.4 regional repeatable work, 3 of 3. NEW COUNTER pallass_fetches_run, frozen at the next tag. Cell (18,4) sits east of forge_station_b, off the bounds lap (rows 2/9, columns 0/25) and off the y=9 lane pallass_walkthrough and pallass_round_trip both use.
entities.observe: A rack of numbered slips beside the second bench: a stock number, a bench number, an hour. No names on any of them. Any pair of hands that can read a gauge can take one down.
entities.once_per_waking_toast: The rack is empty until the next shift files its slips.
entities.toast: You take a slip, walk its stock number down to the racks and the finished piece back up. The clerk who pays you writes down the hour you took, to the quarter.

variants.toast: The smith hands you the slip before the rack does. She says nothing about it. She wouldn't.

entities._comment: v0.16 P1. Cell (15,3) is off every QA lap and assert set, and all four neighbours are open, so no prior save loading here is trapped by the new blocking entity. Full cell audit: the plan's Task 1.2 table.
entities.observe: A wide iron-strapped door standing open on its wedge. Past it: a working hall, and a heat that has its own weather.
A civic bin beside the second bench, half full of work that never left the tier. Each piece has a tag, and every tag has the same examiner's seal on it.
entities.toast: Nine blades in the bin, all from one hand, all failed on the same measure. Somebody up here is doing careful work and failing it the same way every time.

entities.observe: A slate of what the cage is carrying today, chalked by hour. Two lines have been rewritten so many times the slate has gone smooth under them.
entities.toast: One crate of tin, den shop, market tier. Logged three cycles running and carried none of them. Beside it, chalked in a tidier hand: HELD, QUEUE.

entities._comment: P2 HELP leg 1 of 3. once_per_waking books per ENTITY (`serve:<id>`), so three distinct props bank shipment_leg_carried three times in one waking. No lift affordance exists or is being added.
entities.observe: A pallet strapped and tagged and standing exactly where it has stood for three cycles, one hand's width outside the loading square.
entities.once_per_waking_toast: The pallet sits where you put it, squarely inside the loading square.
entities.toast: You get the pallet onto the loading square and the strapping squared. The attendant looks at it, looks at the bell, and says nothing.
